source_review.notes: Checked all 10 structured references against current official Google SRE/Cloud, Apache Flink/Spark, Kubernetes, and FinOps Foundation sources; every final URL returned HTTP 200. Verified current overload, autoscaling, backpressure, scheduler, resource request/limit, BigQuery slot/cost, allocation, unit-economics and FOCUS claims in their stated scopes; provider behavior is treated as implementation evidence rather than universal capacity assurance.

evidence: Checked discrete backlog recurrence, arrival/service/utilization, fluid drain bound, resource capacity envelope, parallel speedup/efficiency, cost conservation and SLO-good unit-cost notation plus balanced GitHub math delimiters.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Notation separates eligible demand, attempts and useful completion; mean utilization and queue behavior; direct/shared/central/unallocated cost; and theoretical from empirical capacity.

evidence: Executed backlog-and-direct-cost and matched backlog 0/20/40/0/0, peak 40, final zero, 500 arrivals/completions, 0.533 worker-hours and $0.064 direct cost.
Recomputed 3.6M backlog over 360 seconds as 10k/s spare, 30k/s total with 20k/s arrivals, and 37.5k/s after 25% aggregate headroom.
numerical_recomputation.notes: All arithmetic is consistent with the declared discrete/fluid assumptions and correctly subtracts continuing arrivals from drain capacity.

evidence: Integrated constant negative backlog derivative while service exceeds arrivals to verify the fluid drain time.
Verified cost equality from an exhaustive disjoint partition of authoritative effective cost records/fractions.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Variable rates, skew, failed work, discreteness, attribution fairness, billing changes and duplicated/missing cost records remain explicit limitations.

evidence: Reviewed burst duration, heterogenous work, hot keys, serial stages, limited partitions, state/checkpoint overlap, sink/dependency quota, startup, scale oscillation, zone loss, replay and retry storms.

Reviewed list/effective rates, credits/commitments, idle reserve, shared/unallocated cost, currency/boundary mismatch, cost shifting, quality/SLO degradation, marginal steps and product retirement residue.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Adversarial analysis spans demand, service, queues, resources, dependencies, elasticity, recovery, accounting, incentives, optimization and lifecycle.

evidence: Traced compatible units/workload, per-stage useful rate, bottleneck/headroom, bounded overload, feasible autoscaling, failure recovery, conserved allocation, SLO-qualified economics and load-test evidence through examples and answers.
invariant_checking.notes: No average, CPU level, worker maximum, queue, benchmark rate, autoscaler, invoice label, allocation, utilization or lower bill is treated as broader proof than it provides.

evidence: Reviewed positive-spare-capacity drain from constant fluid rates and work-conserving service.
Reviewed no-double-count total from disjoint exhaustive allocation categories and shared fractional partitions.
proof_review.notes: Claims are correctly scoped to modeled rates and arithmetic conservation, not stochastic queueing, practical recovery, causal fairness or business value.

evidence: Backlog-drain and cost-conservation statements are explicitly labeled conditional claims and proof sketches with immediate failure conditions.
The executable is labeled a discrete arithmetic illustration and disclaims failures, parallelism, startup, shared cost, billing minimums and SLO proof.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Formal results, deterministic computation, empirical capacity tests, provider documentation and governance decisions remain distinct.

evidence: Current platform/provider behavior is attributed to named official sources and never presented as a portable guarantee.
Benchmarks, load/failure tests, telemetry, forecasts, bills, allocation and before/after savings are framed as scoped evidence requiring common boundaries and guardrails.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: The chapter distinguishes peak from sustainable capacity, attempts from useful output, rate from value, allocation from causation, and savings from hidden degradation.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed end to end. The chapter coherently connects heterogeneous demand to stage bottlenecks, backlog/deadline recovery, bounded overload, autoscaling control, representative capacity testing, conserved attribution, SLO-qualified unit economics, optimization, forecasting and retirement.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed the capacity-and-cost contract, falsifiable claim, twelve-step mechanism, stage/resource inventory, workload classes, load/failure matrix, autoscaling controls, cost taxonomy, allocation conservation, ten examples and estate recovery for operational usability.

pedagogical_review.notes: Reviewed progression from one-page model through prerequisites, demand, bottlenecks, sizing, overload, autoscaling, tests, attribution, unit economics, optimization, portfolio planning, notation, two conditional proofs, executable, 14 trade-offs, 25 misconceptions, ten examples and five complete answers. Connections accurately retrieve DE-035/049/063/073-074/091-096, API-071/073-075 and PLAT-073/077/082/089 and prepare DE-098.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
